name: Slav Defence
summary: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6: Black guards d5 with a pawn instead of ...e6, so the light-squared bishop can still go to f5 or g4 before the pawn chain closes. A solid centre, clear plans, and a good answer to every White system.

black: Guard d5 with ...c6, not ...e6: the c8 bishop stays free.
Develop the c8 bishop to f5 or g4 first, then play ...e6. The bishop is then outside the chain c6, d5, e6.
After ...dxc4, give the pawn back on good terms: use the time White spends to win it back to develop.
Against the Exchange, develop the same way as White until the position is safe, then use the open c-file.
white: Play 5.a4 after ...dxc4 to stop ...b5 holding the pawn, then win the c4 pawn back.
Chase the f5 bishop with Nh4 or Ne5 and win the bishop pair.
Hit b7 with Qb3 when the c8 bishop has left it unguarded.
Gain central space with e4 when Black's pieces are not ready to hit it.

structures.name: The Slav chain: c6, d5, e6 with the bishop outside
structures.text: Black's pawns on c6, d5 and e6 are on light squares and very hard to break. A bishop inside that chain has no moves, so Black puts it on f5 or g4 before ...e6. That one detail is the whole difference from the Queen's Gambit Declined.

structures.name: Exchange Slav: symmetrical d-pawns
structures.text: After cxd5 cxd5 both sides have a centre pawn on the d-file and the c-file is open. The position is quiet: the side that uses the c-file first, and keeps the pieces active, gets the edge.

structures.name: Semi-Slav: ...e6 before the bishop comes out
structures.text: If Black plays ...e6 and ...c6 with the bishop still on c8, the lichess book calls it the Semi-Slav, a separate opening. The bishop is shut in, but Black gets ...dxc4 and ...b5 ideas instead. This course plays the bishop out first.

black: c8 bishop: f5 or g4 before ...e6; it is the reason for 2...c6.
f6 knight: guards d5 and the kingside, and hits e4.
b8 knight: d7 to support ...e5 or ...c5, or a6 towards b4 after a4.
Queen: b6 or c7 when White's queen comes to b3.
white: f3 knight: h4 or e5 to chase the f5 bishop.
a-pawn: a4 stops ...b5 holding the extra c4 pawn.
Queen: b3 hits b7, which the f5 bishop no longer guards.
e-pawn: e3 for a solid centre, e4 for a big one.

lines.name: Main line, 5.a4 Bf5: the bishop goes first
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5 6. e3 e6 7. Bxc4 Bb4 8. O-O Nbd7 9. Qe2 Bg6 10. e4 O-O 11. Bd3 Bh5 12. e5 Nd5 13. Nxd5 cxd5

notes.2...c6: Guards d5 with a pawn and keeps the c8 bishop free.
notes.4...dxc4: Takes the pawn. White must spend time to win it back, and Black develops in that time.
notes.5.a4: Stops ...b5, which would hold the extra pawn. The cost: a hole on b4.
notes.5...Bf5: The bishop leaves before ...e6 closes the diagonal.
notes.6.e3: Opens the f1 bishop's diagonal to take back on c4.
notes.6...e6: Now ...e6 is free: the bishop is already outside the chain.
notes.7...Bb4: Uses the b4 hole that a4 made and pins the c3 knight, which guards e4.
notes.9.Qe2: Prepares e4 with the queen behind it.
notes.9...Bg6: The bishop leaves f5 before the e4 push attacks it.
notes.11...Bh5: Pins the f3 knight to the queen.
notes.12.e5: Gains space and kicks the f6 knight.
notes.12...Nd5: The knight goes to d5, where no White pawn can attack it.
notes.13...cxd5: Black has a solid pawn on d5 and the c-file is open for a rook.

lines.name: Krause Attack, 6.Ne5: hit back with ...e5
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5 6. Ne5 Nbd7 7. Nxc4 Qc7 8. g3 e5 9. dxe5 Nxe5 10. Bf4 Nfd7 11. Bg2 f6

notes.6.Ne5: Hits c4 and prepares f3 and e4.
notes.6...Nbd7: Challenges the e5 knight at once.
notes.8.g3: Prepares Bg2 and Bf4 against the e5 square.
notes.8...e5: Strikes the centre: the f5 bishop is outside the chain, so ...e5 does not block it.
notes.10.Bf4: Pins the e5 knight against the queen on c7.
notes.11...f6: A third defender of e5. The bishop on f5 keeps the light squares guarded.

lines.name: Exchange Slav: symmetry and the c-file
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. Nc3 Nf6 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. Bf4 Bf5 7. e3 e6 8. Qb3 Bb4 9. Bb5 O-O 10. Bxc6 Bxc3+ 11. Qxc3 Rc8

notes.3.cxd5: Symmetrical pawns. White hopes the extra move counts.
notes.5...Nc6: Hits d4 and keeps the position equal.
notes.6...Bf5: The bishop comes out before ...e6, as always in the Slav.
notes.8.Qb3: Hits b7, which the bishop on f5 no longer guards.
notes.8...Bb4: Pins the c3 knight, a guard of d5 and e4.
notes.9.Bb5: Pins the c6 knight and threatens Bxc6.
notes.10...Bxc3+: Take first, so that after Qxc3 the rook comes to c8 with tempo.
notes.11...Rc8: The rook hits the c6 bishop on the open c-file; the b7 pawn attacks it too.

lines.name: Chebanenko, 4...a6: prepare ...b5
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 a6 5. e3 b5 6. b3 Bg4 7. Be2 Nbd7 8. O-O e6 9. h3 Bh5 10. Bb2 Bd6

notes.4...a6: Prepares ...b5, which gains queenside space and can take on c4 with a pawn behind it.
notes.5...b5: Hits c4 and asks White to decide.
notes.6.b3: Keeps the c4 pawn guarded so ...dxc4 does not win it.
notes.6...Bg4: The bishop comes out before ...e6 and pins the f3 knight.
notes.8...e6: Now ...e6: the bishop is outside the chain.
notes.9...Bh5: Keeps the bishop on the diagonal to f3 instead of trading it for the knight.
notes.10...Bd6: Develops and prepares to castle; Black's queenside pawns give space.

lines.name: Quiet Variation, 4.e3 Bf5: the bishop pair for the h-file
lines.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 Bf5 5. Nc3 e6 6. Nh4 Bg6 7. Nxg6 hxg6 8. Bd3 Nbd7 9. O-O Bd6 10. h3 O-O

notes.4.e3: Solid, but it shuts in White's c1 bishop.
notes.4...Bf5: The bishop goes out while the diagonal is open.
notes.6.Nh4: Chases the bishop to win the bishop pair.
notes.6...Bg6: Black lets White take, because hxg6 opens the h-file for Black's rook.
notes.7...hxg6: Doubled pawns, but they guard f5 and h5 and the h-file is half-open.
notes.8.Bd3: Hits g6; it is guarded by the f7 pawn.
notes.10...O-O: Black is solid; ...dxc4 and ...e5 come next.

traps.name: Exchange Slav, 7...Nb4?: the fork that fails
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. Bf4 Nc6 5. e3 Bf5 6. Qb3 e6 7. Qxb7 Nb4 8. Bb5+ Nc6 9. Bxc6+ Qd7 10. Qxd7#

notes.6.Qb3: Hits b7, which the f5 bishop no longer guards.
notes.7...Nb4: The mistake: it threatens ...Nc2+, a fork of king and rook. But the knight leaves c6, and the a4-e8 diagonal opens to the king.

traps.punishment: 8.Bb5+ mates in three: 8...Nc6 9.Bxc6+ Qd7 10.Qxd7 is mate. 7...Bb4+ was the better move; White keeps the extra pawn, but there is no mate.

traps.name: Alekhine Variation, 7.Ne4?: the knight with no guard
traps.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. e3 b5 6. a4 b4 7. Ne4 Nxe4

notes.5...b5: Without a4 already played, ...b5 holds the extra pawn.
notes.6.a4: Attacks b5 to break the chain.
notes.6...b4: Pushes on and hits the c3 knight.
notes.7.Ne4: The mistake: it looks active, but nothing guards e4.

traps.punishment: 7...Nxe4 wins a whole knight. The e3 pawn guards d4 and f4, not e4, and the f1 bishop is still at home. 7.Na2 keeps the knight.
